transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, the main reason I'm here is that I'm having a really hard time with my job lately. I'm a medical services manager, and anything that takes real, sitting-down brain work—like putting together monthly reports or planning a multi-site health event—it just feels like I hit a wall. I keep putting it off, even when I know it's important and needs to get done. It's just getting too hard to manage.
How long have you been dealing with this kind of difficulty getting started and staying focused on these tasks?

It's been going on for about a year and eleven months now. It really started right after a friend of mine passed away. When that happened, I ended up taking on more of the league and outreach responsibilities, and... yeah, ever since then, it's just been a struggle to get through it all.
During this time, have you also been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless?

No, not really. I mean, obviously I was very sad when my friend passed away, but... I haven't been feeling persistently down or hopeless or anything like that in general. It's really just frustration with myself because I can't seem to just sit down and get my work done.
Looking back at your childhood and school years, did you have similar difficulties with attention, focus, or getting things done?

Yeah, I actually did. Even way back in elementary school, my teachers used to tell my parents that I was bright, but... I was always daydreaming. I was constantly losing my worksheets or just forgetting to turn in my homework. Honestly, the only way my assignments actually got turned in was because my mother checked my backpack every single night to make sure I had everything.
